title: Rwanda Launches World's First National Drone Delivery Network
reason: Fully corroborated by multiple independent, high-authority sources. President Paul Kagame launched the service in Muhanga District on 14 October 2016 (GlobeNewswire's press release/dateline of 13 Oct refers to the announcement immediately preceding the ceremony reported elsewhere as 14 Oct — a one-day dateline discrepancy, not material). Operator confirmed as California-based Zipline. Gavi, Zipline's own newsroom, and the original GlobeNewswire release all confirm: up to 150 on-demand emergency deliveries per day, to 21 transfusion facilities in western Rwanda, each drone flying up to 150km round trip carrying 1.5kg of blood. The December 2016 life-saving case is also independently confirmed: on 21 December 2016, a 2-year-old girl (Ghislane Ihimbazwe) suffering severe malaria-induced blood loss received a drone-delivered blood transfusion credited with saving her life (reported by multiple outlets including a detailed account matching the description). All material details (actor, location, year, scope, magnitude) match the event description precisely.

A week later, on 24 December 1978, Habyarimana ran unopposed in a presidential election and won with 98.99% of votes cast (matches the described "98%" support). The regime's entrenchment of northern Hutu (Gisenyi/akazu network) domination of state institutions and the military, replacing the prior southern Hutu-dominated Kayibanda regime, is independently corroborated by Wikipedia, Britannica, HRW, and Grokipedia. All material elements (country, year, constitution, referendum, MRND single-party institutionalization, ~98% Habyarimana vote share, northern Hutu domination of state/military) check out.
